target_customer: Medical device manufacturers that must build cybersecurity into regulated devices
problem: Connected devices such as pacemakers and pumps need security features and regulatory compliance that device makers lack in house.
business_model: B2B software licensed to device OEMs, with fleet monitoring and threat sharing

founders.name: Mike Kijewski
previous_startups: Gamma Basics (acquired by Varian Medical Systems, 2013)
founders.background_notes: Described as having over a decade in cybersecurity and cryptography. Co-founded Gamma Basics earlier.

founders.name: Eric Pancoast
previous_startups: Gamma Basics (acquired by Varian Medical Systems, 2013)

competitors.name: Medigate
competitors.what: Medical IoT device security and asset visibility for hospitals
competitors.funding_then: $5.35M seed in late 2017 and $15M Series A in January 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: Embedded security toolkit for regulated devices plus a cloud monitoring network, needing cryptography skill and alignment with FDA expectations.

defensibility.rationale: Once embedded in a device design the toolkit is costly to swap, and pooled telemetry adds value, but peers were funded.

incumbents: Medical device OEMs in house teams
takeover_risk_then.outcome: Device makers became customers and investors (J&J, Intuitive, Dexcom) rather than building it themselves, based on the 2022 and 2023 rounds.

market_need_then: Rising attention to connected device attacks and FDA premarket cybersecurity expectations created demand from device makers around 2018 and 2019.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive of medicine plus crypto and clear to buyers, but no sourced brand assets or community beyond trade press.

outcome_analysis: MedCrypt sold to device makers facing rising security expectations and raised a $5.3M Series A in 2019 and a $25M Series B in November 2022 with strategic medical device investors, extended by Dexcom Ventures in January 2023. Founders had a prior health software exit, and device manufacturers backing it signals real demand. It is still active.
notes: Series A lead and amount come from search summaries of 2019 coverage and should be rechecked. Early seed money before 2019 not found, so coverage is partial. Total raised reported as about $34M after Series B and $36.4M after the Dexcom extension. Name origin not found. Website redirects from medcrypt.co to medcrypt.com.
